extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, practitioners, and USPTO staff preparing or filing sequence listings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for creating, representing, validating, and filing WIPO ST.26-compliant sequence listings (Sequence Listing XML) with the USPTO (37 CFR 1.831-1.835).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for Sequence Listing XML (37 CFR 1.831)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides the requirement for a sequence listing in XML format using the term 'Sequence Listing XML.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.831 requires sequence listings to be in ST.26 XML format (referred to as 'Sequence Listing XML'). This implements WIPO Standard ST.26 for applications filed on or after July 1, 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which nucleotides and amino acids must be included or prohibited (37 CFR 1.831)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines which nucleotides and amino acids must be included and which are prohibited from being included in the 'Sequence Listing XML.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation incorporates ST.26 rules specifying mandatory inclusion of certain residue types (e.g., nucleotide analogs, D-amino acids) and prohibits certain short sequence entries (see separate criterion on minimum length). Consult 1.831 text and ST.26 for exact lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sequence identifier text (e.g., 'SEQ ID NO:')
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides the requirement to use a sequence identifier, i.e., 'SEQ ID NO:' or the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sequence must be given a sequence identifier label in the listing. Use consistent identifier formatting (e.g., 'SEQ ID NO:') so sequences are unambiguously identified in application text and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequential numbering of sequences (37 CFR 1.832)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequences in the listing must be assigned a separate sequence identifier beginning with 1 and increasing sequentially by integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number sequence entries starting at 1 and incrementing by 1 for each subsequent sequence. Do not skip or duplicate identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and symbols for nucleotide/amino acid residues (37 CFR 1.832)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for the required representation and symbols to be used for identifying nucleotide and amino acid residues in a 'Sequence Listing XML.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ST.26-prescribed residue symbols and representations. This includes handling of mixed-specified/unspecified residue regions, use of 'n' and 'X', and symbol conventions for residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for complex sequence types (non-contiguous, n/X regions, gaps) (37 CFR 1.832)
rubrics_metrics.description: Governs representation and symbols used for nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences that may be: (1) a single continuous sequence derived from one or more non-contiguous segments of a larger sequence, (2) sequences that contain regions of specifically defined residues separated by one or more regions of contiguous specified 'n' or 'X' residues, or (3) a sequence that contains regions of specifically defined residues separated by one or more gaps of an unknown or undisclosed number of residues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ST.26 XML constructs and symbol conventions to represent joined segments, regions with 'n'/'X' placeholders, and unknown-length gaps. Ensure the chosen representation conforms to the ST.26 DTD and USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-file requirement and Unicode UTF-8 encoding (37 CFR 1.833 / 1.834)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires that the 'Sequence Listing XML' is in a single file encoded using Unicode UTF-8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the sequence listing as one UTF-8 encoded XML file. Do not split the listing across multiple files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity according to ST.26 DTD (37 CFR 1.833)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires that the 'Sequence Listing XML' be valid according to the DTD (document type definition) of WIPO Standard ST.26 in Annex II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate the XML against the ST.26 DTD (Annex II) before filing. Non-valid XML can trigger USPTO non-compliance notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required XML components (37 CFR 1.833)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies the components of the 'Sequence Listing XML' by incorporating certain paragraphs of ST.26 as: (1) an XML declaration; (2) a document type declaration; (3) a root element; (4) a general information part; and (5) a sequence data part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the XML includes each required top-level component exactly as ST.26 specifies so the file adheres structurally to the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of language-dependent free text (37 CFR 1.833 / 1.834)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires that language-dependent, free text elements are in the English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within the Sequence Listing XML, any free-text elements that are language-dependent must be provided in English for filing with the USPTO. Note: some other IP offices may require translations into the language of filing for their records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content: file naming, extension, compression, printable characters (37 CFR 1.834)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides the form and content of the 'Sequence Listing XML,' identifies computer compatibility as well as file extension, naming convention parameters to be used and how and when file compression may be used, and provides for the number of permitted printable characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow USPTO-prescribed filename conventions and file extensions; compress only to non-self-extracting archives when submitting on optical media; observe character limits and permitted printable characters defined in the regulations/annex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing channels and size limits (Patent Center or physical media)
rubrics_metrics.description: ST.26 sequence listings in XML format MUST be filed electronically with the USPTO through Patent Center or on physical media. EFS-Web will not permit submission of ST.26 XML files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Patent Center for electronic submission (Patent Center recognizes XML file format and auto-adds document description). Patent Center accepts XML files 100 MB or less; larger submissions must be on read-only optical discs (CD/DVD) and may be compressed (non-self-extracting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference statement required in the specification (37 CFR 1.77(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings in ST.26 XML format must be accompanied by an incorporation by reference statement (for 111(a) applications), which includes the name of the file, the date of creation, and the size of the file in bytes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit incorporation-by-reference statement in the specification naming the XML file, stating its creation date and byte size. Paper or PDF copies are not required and are counted toward application size fees if provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amending application to add or replace Sequence Listing XML (37 CFR 1.835)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides the procedure for amending an application to add a 'Sequence Listing XML' or replace a 'Sequence Listing XML' along with the necessary identification of support for additions, deletions or replacements of sequence information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding or replacing the listing, include statements of no new matter and statements showing support for the changes made. Be prepared to respond to USPTO notices of non-compliance per the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and response rules for non-compliance (37 CFR 1.835)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides the basis for the issuance of notices when non-compliance is raised, and the rules for responding to such notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the USPTO determines the Sequence Listing XML does not comply, it may issue a notice; follow the procedural response requirements and supply corrected/justifying materials as allowed under the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition applicability dates and grandfathering (effective July 1, 2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications with a filing date or international filing date BEFORE July 1, 2022 MUST file sequence listings in ST.25 format; All applications with a filing date or international filing date ON OR AFTER July 1, 2022 MUST file sequence listings in ST.26 format. There will be no 'grandfathering' for filings claiming benefit or priority to earlier applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 111(a) apps use the official filing date; for U.S. national phase (371) apps use the PCT filing date as the relevant date. Provisional applications are not required to include sequence listings, but if submitted after July 1, 2022 they must comply with ST.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earliest priority/application and applicant/inventor name rules (ST.25 vs ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under ST.26 ONLY the earliest priority application can be included; ONLY one applicant AND optionally ONE inventor may be included; multiple invention titles are permitted, each one in a different language; applicant/inventor names may be included using any valid Unicode character along with a basic Latin translation or transliteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ST.26 restricts how priority, applicant, and inventor information is represented compared to ST.25. Include only the earliest priority application and follow Unicode/basic Latin translation rules for names and titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence types and annotation requirements (ST.25 vs ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: ST.25 used ASCII text with numeric identifiers and allowed limited annotation; ST.26 uses XML with elements and attributes, requires annotation for feature keys and qualifiers, and permits additional sequence types (e.g., branched sequences, nucleotide analogs, D-amino acids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ST.26's structured XML allows more precise feature annotation (keys and qualifiers) and inclusion of sequence types not covered by ST.25. Do not use 'mixed mode'; include translations only in 'translation' qualifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum-length prohibition for very short sequences (ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: ST.26 prohibits sequences shorter than certain thresholds: specifically, sequences of <10 specifically defined nucleotides and <4 specifically defined amino acids are prohibited in the sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include entries for sequence fragments that fall below the ST.26 minimum-length thresholds in the Sequence Listing XML. Such short sequences were allowed under ST.25 but are prohibited under ST.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default handling for 'n' and 'X' variables (ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'n' and 'X' variables default value assumed with no definition; ST.26 does not require a definition provided in a feature key as ST.25 did.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'n' or 'X' placeholders are used without explicit definitions, ST.26 assumes default values—follow ST.26 conventions rather than providing per-feature definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict feature location formats and permitted location operators (ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strictly defined feature location formats permit the use of '<' and '>' in all sequence types and '^', 'join', 'order', 'complement' in nucleotide sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these permitted operators and location notations exactly as ST.26 prescribes when specifying feature locations in the XML; incorrect location formatting can lead to invalid XML or non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mixed-mode sequence presentation; use 'translation' qualifiers for translations
rubrics_metrics.description: No 'mixed mode' is permitted (i.e., nucleotide translation shown inline); nucleotide translations are included in 'translation' qualifiers only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present mixed-mode sequences (showing amino acid translation inline). Put translations into the dedicated 'translation' qualifier fields in the XML.

rubrics_metrics.name: ST.26 improves data compatibility with INSDC and standardizes feature keys/qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Data compatibility with the INSDC requirements, namely sequence annotations and organism names will be included in publicly searchable databases; standardization of feature keys, feature locations, qualifiers, qualifier values, and sequence variant presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting to ST.26 facilitates exchange with GenBank/INSDC and improves discoverability. Use standardized feature keys and qualifier values per ST.26 to enable database ingestion and interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO Sequence tool recommended for authoring, validation, and generation
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO Sequence is a desktop tool developed by WIPO to support authoring, validation, and generation of ST.26-compliant sequence listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use WIPO Sequence to simplify creation of ST.26 XML (no need to edit XML directly), validate project data and existing XML, generate compliant XML and human-readable versions, and import various file types (ST.25, ST.26, FASTA, etc.). It is free from WIPO's standards site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing metadata and submission practice (paper/PDF are not required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper or PDF copies of the sequence listing are NOT required; any paper or pdf copies are considered part of the specification for calculating application size fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer submitting only the required XML via Patent Center or optical disc and include the incorporation-by-reference metadata to avoid unnecessary PDF/paper copies that may increase application size fees.
